title_original: John Leguizamo, Indya Moore and D’Arcy Carden to be Honored at Denver Film Festival

blocks.text: John Leguizamo , Indya Moore and D’Arcy Carden will be honored at the 49th Denver Film Festival , which runs Oct. 22—Nov. 1.

Leguizamo will receive the John Cassavetes Award presented by Next50. The actor will make an appearance at the festival on Oct. 30 to accept the honor prior to a newly added screening of Christopher Nolan’s “The Odyssey,” in which Leguizamo starred as Eumaeus.

blocks.text: Indya Moore will receive the CinemaQ LaBahn Ikon Award at the Denver Art Museum on Oct. 25. The actress, model, writer and producer — known for her role as Angel on FX’s “Pose” — will participate in a moderated conversation with Jill D’Allessandro, curator for the museum’s “DIVA” exhibit, which runs Oct. 4—Jan. 31, 2027.
D’Arcy Carden (“The Good Place, “The Five-Star Weekend”) will receive the Women+Film Barbara Bridges Inspiration Award at the Festival’s Awards Brunch on Nov. 1.
Popular on Variety

“We couldn’t be more excited to welcome three extraordinary artists whose talent, creativity and impact extend far beyond the screen,” said Matthew Campbell, Denver Film Festival artistic director. “John Leguizamo has built a remarkable career defined by fearless performances, incredible range and the independent spirit that makes him such a deserving recipient of our Cassavetes Award. Indya Moore is a groundbreaking artist and powerful voice for representation and inclusion, while D’Arcy Carden brings an exceptional combination of comedic brilliance, versatility and heart to everything she does. Each has made a unique and lasting mark on the entertainment industry, and we’re thrilled to celebrate their achievements and give Denver audiences the opportunity to connect with these inspiring artists during this year’s Festival.”
The DFF program will also include six Creative Conversations with filmmakers and industry experts. The discussions will be held in the lower level of The Tattered Cover and include:
Screenwriting with Peter Gamble — Oct. 23 at 11:30 a.m. Peter Gamble screenwriter, “I Play Rocky”

When the Buses Arrived — Oct. 27 at 11 a.m. Al Jackson, moderator Andrea Ryall, founder, Hope Has No Borders Karen Orona, communications manager at the Colorado Immigrants’ Rights Coalition Jon Ewing, press secretary for the Denver Mayor’s Office Rebekah Henderson and Lilah Park, filmmakers

Muddy Waters – Navigating the Colorado River’s Uncertain Future — Oct. 27 at 1 p.m. Tahlia Bear, moderator Mara Tasker, director, “The River” Lorelei Cloud, film participant and water activist Jim Lochhead, former CEO of Denver Water Perry Cabot, CSU Extension professor and water expert

The Evolving Television Landscape, presented by SeriesFest — Oct. 29, 12:30 p.m. John Wenzel, moderator and Denver Post journalist Teri Weinberg, president, Yellow Brick Road Alex Maggioni, head of television at LAIKA Live Action Elsie Choi, founder and executive producer, Hours and Seasons
Costume Design with Mona May — Oct. 30, 11 a.m. Mona May, costume designer, “Clueless”
Casting Director Karlee Formalont — Oct. 30, 1 p.m. Karlee Formalont, casting director, “A Complete Unknown,” “The Post”
DFF49 will also screen and judge selected films in competition. Jurors for this year’s in-competitions films include:
Krzysztof Kieslowski Award for Best Feature Film David Canfield, The Hollywood Reporter Destiny Jackson, Deadline Rochelle Rose, national director, Performers Program, SAG-AFTRA Foundation
Maysles Brothers Award for Best Documentary Justine Suzanne Jones, producer Ryan Lattanzio, IndieWire Chris Murphy, Vanity Fair
True Grit Award Ethan Alter, Gold Derby Karlee Fomalont, casting director Danielle Rose Russell, actress
Shorts Competitions Kate Chamuris, producer Mona May, costume designer Darwin Shaw, producer
